conviction_note: The quarter should land near its guide on comps that pricing carries (Take 5 sped up in the same months), but the street's Q4 EPS of $0.42 sits above the $0.35-0.40 the FY26 guide implies. The FY27 guide is the swing: Group III base-oil postings rose again on Sept 1 and Oct 1, and RBC expects a 'fairly conservative' guide against a street FY27 EPS near $1.94. Three things work against that downside: a 12%-of-float short, a $500M buyback that resumes after the results, and last year's below-street guide that cost only 2.5%. That leaves p_up at 46 on a 6% scale (-0.48), and the findings' own sum is -0.8. Both are small and negative.

findings.finding: The street's Q4 bar sits above what the company's own FY26 guide implies. findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the $0.42 and the $1.75 FY figure, but none does the arithmetic against the YTD actuals. If the market had priced a Q4 at the guide top ($0.40) as a miss, the stock would not have run 37% off its September low into the print.

findings.finding: Take 5 Oil Change (Driven Brands), the closest quick-lube rival, posted preliminary same-store sales of +4.9% for Jul-Sep 2026, up from +3.6% in Apr-Jun. That is an acceleration in exactly Valvoline's fiscal Q4 months, consistent with industry-wide pass-through pricing. Valvoline's FY comp guide of 7.5-8% against 7.3% YTD (5.8/8.2/8.0) implies Q4 comps of about 9-10%. Valvoline has run about 4.4 points above Take 5 (8.0 vs 3.6 in Apr-Jun), which on 4.9% gives about 9.3%, inside the implied range.
findings.link: Same service (drive-through quick-lube oil change), same consumer, overlapping US markets. Take 5 is Valvoline's largest direct competitor in the format; the quarters line up exactly (Take 5 Q3 ended Sep 26, VVV fiscal Q4 ended Sep 30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comps above guide helped: Q2 FY26 comps of 8.2% with a raised guide gave +4.98%. In Q3, comps of 8.0% and a raised comp guide still gave -5.86% because margins dominated.
findings.why_not_priced: The DRVN release was read for its restatement and guide cut, not for what Take 5's acceleration says about VVV's quarter. If it had been priced into VVV, the comp line would not still be framed as the 'key test' in VVV previews.

findings.finding: Group III base-oil costs kept rising after Valvoline last spoke. Motiva raised Group II+/III postings $1.00/gal on Sept 1, SK Enmove +$0.50/gal on Sept 8, and Motiva +$0.75/gal (4cst) and +$0.50/gal (6/8cst) on Oct 1. A US distributor declared force majeure on Middle East base oils, and Argus called Group III prices record highs into September and October. In August management said 'price and cost should be back in balance' by the end of Q4 and that costs persist 4-6 months after Hormuz reopens. Hormuz traffic was at its lowest since May in early September. That points to Q4 compression at the wide end of 300-400bp and an H1 FY27 cost lag in the first guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin guidance drives this stock. The Aug 5 2026 Q4 margin-compression call sent a beat to -5.86%, and the Nov 2025 below-street FY26 EPS guide gave -2.48%.
findings.why_not_priced: Postings come from a trade press most equity investors do not read. If the market had priced costs still rising in late Q4, the stock would not have run from $26 to $36 between late September and early November on a cost-normalising narrative.
findings.independence: Argus, 2026-09-29, on Motiva's Oct 1 increase (https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2884511-motiva-raises-group-ii-ii-iii-base-oil-posted-prices; page body did not load, headline and search snippet only). Argus, 2026-10-08, on record Group III prices (https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/market-opinion-and-analysis-blog/european-base-oils-group-iii-price-pressure, snippet). Korea Times, 2026-09-07, on Hormuz traffic (https://koreatimes.co.kr/world/20260907/hormuz-traffic-dips-to-lowest-since-may-after-us-iranian-strikes-on-ships). Counterweights, already netted into the size: Stifel puts finished lubricants at about 12% of revenue with strong pass-through (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/valvoline-shares-jump-stifel-upgrades-143217001.html, 2026-03-23); Chevron Pascagoula Group III was due to start in October 2026; and management said prices historically do not roll back. Shrunk for the 12% short.

findings.finding: Lower-income consumer pressure in the quick-lube category is building into FY27. Driven Brands cut Take 5's FY comp guide to 3.5-4.0% (implying deceleration in Oct-Dec from 4.9%), citing 'continued pressure on lower-income consumers across Take 5'. Gasoline was $4.48/gal in late September. Monro's maintenance services fell 5% in Apr-Jun, with high gas prices blamed. Valvoline itself flagged softer lower-income traffic in June. Transaction counts and the FY27 comp guide are exposed.
findings.link: Take 5 is the same service and the same customer, and its Oct-Dec quarter equals Valvoline's FY27 Q1. Monro is general automotive maintenance; oil change is not broken out (link weaker).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 commentary on lower-income softness came on a day the stock fell -5.86%, though margins were the main driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews treat VVV's comp guide as safe because pricing carries it. A rival's guide cut on lower-income traffic says transaction counts, which the market watches, may turn negative in the FY27 guide.

findings.finding: Competing DIY and big-box oil prices rose far more than Valvoline's stated $5-7 per oil change. Costco's Kirkland 10-quart oil went from $22 in May to $58 by late September, Costco rationed motor oil to two purchases a week, and Walmart raised its oil-change price 'a few dollars' in August. That gives Valvoline a pricing umbrella and possibly some DIY-to-service shift. The same article notes some drivers now bring their own oil.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on competitor pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: Consumer-press pricing anecdotes are not modelled into VVV's ticket or transaction counts. This is a proxy with one store's price points, so it is sized small.
